correctness.rationale: For cyclic p-power groups over characteristic p, K[C_m]=K[z]/z^m. Both automorphisms alpha and beta preserve all powers z^a. Right ideal closure under star with 1 forces alpha(I)=I, then multiplication with arbitrary star-right factors proves I is a ring ideal; the left side follows dually with beta. Thus the complete ideal chain and products J^a star J^b=J^(a+b) are proved for arbitrary fields. Exact finite verifier verifies all chain levels for m=3,5,9 and all 28 subspaces when m=3; finite checks are supplementary.

originality.rationale: Zhang 2026 supplies the transported product and augmentation-power formula but not exhaustion of one-sided ideals. The semisimple dihedral representation decomposition in Elhamdadi-Fernando-Tsvelikhovskiy, Proposition 4.18, assumes real or complex coefficients. Bardakov-Elhamdadi 2026 treats augmentation powers mainly with integral coefficients; Sangare-Ta 2026 concerns idempotents, automorphisms and commutators. The fresh contribution is the complete *simultaneous* left/right/two-sided chain and its ideal multiplication for all fields of defining characteristic over cyclic prime-power Latin quandles. A standard representation-theoretic derivation elsewhere is an explicit residual novelty risk.
residual_risks: An equivalent unindexed modular permutation-module classification may predate this proof or follow as an implicit corollary in literature not inspected.
No external independent audit; full-spectrum literature exhaustiveness and priority are not established.

value.rationale: The complete one-sided and two-sided ideal lattice and its exact product calculus are natural structural invariants across an infinite defining-characteristic family of nonassociative quandle algebras. The uniserial nilpotent augmentation chain is a sharp contrast with the split semisimple case; the field-uniform classification may guide modular representations and ideal-based invariants. The required cyclic/Latin hypotheses are structurally motivated, not arbitrary enumeration.
